newsitem.title: USA: Dlr rise on Lebed ouster seen limited - US experts.
newsitem.headline: Dlr rise on Lebed ouster seen limited - US experts.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin's decision to fire National Security Chief Alexander Lebed sent investors scurrying to buy the U.S. currency, but dollar gains are expected to be limited, analysts said.
"The sentiment for the dollar is really very positive anyway right now," said Gabriele Lamers, an international economist at Bank of Boston.
"(Lebed's dismissal) is just one of those other things that is helping the dollar at the moment," she added.
Yeltsin announced Lebed's ouster on national television on Thursday.

The news came on the heels of allegations by Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov on Wednesday that Lebed had been plotting a "creeping coup" while the Russian President prepared for heart surgery. Lebed denied the accusation.
Shortly after the announcement, the dollar surged to 1.5454 marks, a fresh 4-1/2-month high, and then slipped to trade around 1.5430.
The mark often suffers amid Russian political turmoil because of Germany's close economic ties to Russia.
The Swiss franc, also considered a safe haven currency, gained ground against the mark.
Lamers predicted the dollar will likely hold above 1.54 marks for the remainder of the day in light of events in Russia.
Technicians deemed 1.5487 marks, a high from May, as the dollar's upside objective. The dollar hit a double peak of 1.5488 and 1.5487 marks on May 28 and May 29, repectively.
MMS International Inc technical analyst Ken Boyer said he expects the dollar to come within "striking distance" of 1.5487 marks.
"However, that's also very good resistance and that should result in some profit taking and consolidation and pull back before I'd consider a break higher," Boyer added.
Yeltsin's health concerns have kept his presidency under a cloud. The Kremlin announced this week that doctors will operate on Yeltsin's heart in mid-November.
"Yeltsin's health is still a problem, and what would happen if he were to die is a big question mark overhanging the market," said Chris Widness, an international economist at Chase Securities Inc.
Widness emphasized that Lebed's firing on Thursday does not lift concern about the health of the Russian leader.
"It removes one uncertainty, but there is so much uncertainty in Russia anyway that I think it's such a marginal event," Widness said.
